Order on Criminal Misc. Application No. 3 of 2025
1.
By order dated 14.3.2018 an amount of Rs. 20,000/- was directed to be deposited by the applicant no. 1 with the Mediation Centre in respect of mediation proceedings.
As per the Mediation Centre report, applicant no. 1 has deposited the aforesaid amount, however, opposite party no. 2 failed to appear on all the dates.
2. In view of the aforesaid, the amount of Rs. 20,000/- deposited by the applicant no. 1 with the Mediation Centre be returned to the applicant no. 1-Prashant Alias Hani within fifteen days.
3. Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 has no objection.
4. Accordingly, the application is allowed.
Order on Application 1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants/revisionist, learned counsel for opposite party no.2 and learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. Application No. 8189 of 2018 under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashing the entire criminal proceeding of Criminal Case No. 10642/IX/2017 (State Vs. Prashant and others) arising out of Case Crime No.490 of 2016 including charge sheet dated 18.04.2017 under Sections 498A,
323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Govind Nagar, District Mathura, pending in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Mathura.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants/revisionist submitted that divorce by mutual consent has been granted by order dated 9.12.2024 passed by the Family Court, which is annexed at page no. 26 of the supplementary affidavit and in view of the divorce decree, the present case be finally decided.
4. Learned counsel for opposite party no.2 has not disputed the facts as stated by learned counsel for the applicants/revisionist.
He further contended that opposite party no.2 does not want to proceed with the criminal case against the applicants/revisionist and the same may be quashed.
5. Learned AGA does not dispute the fact that parties and he would have no objection in case criminal proceedings are put to an end.
He further submits that in view of settlement there is virtually no chance of any conviction being recorded in the criminal proceedings.

6. Having examined the matter in its totality, this Court is of the view that the criminal proceedings in the present case had essentially been an outcome of a matrimonial dispute and there are no such Prashant Alias Hani And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: Needless to observe that with the present stand of the parties in terms of their settlement, there is practically no chance of recording conviction, even if the case under the F.I.R. in question is put to trial.
In other words, entire exercise of trial would only be an exercise in futility.

On the contrary, looking to the nature of dispute and the fact that the disputants have compromised and want to proceed peacefully ahead, it would be in the interest of justice that criminal proceedings in question are quashed.

7. It would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice

,
it is appropriate that the criminal case is put to an end.

8. In view of the fact that the parties do not want to pursue the case any further as stated by them and the fact that matter has been mutually settled between the parties in view of the divorce decree order dated 9.12.2024 passed by the Family Court, no useful purpose would be served in proceeding with the matter further.

9. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Parbatbhai Aahir Vs. State of Gujarat (2017) 9 SCC 641, Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303 and State of M.P. Vs. Laxmi Narayan, (2019) 5 SCC 688, the proceedings of the aforesaid case (as detailed in paragraph no. 2) is hereby quashed and the judgment/order dated 3.1.2022 passed by Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Mathura (as detailed in paragraph no. 2-A) is hereby quashed.
